newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - March 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

ACTU assistant secretary Greg Combet said yesterday union membership at Comalco Ltd's Queensland bauxite mining operations at Weipa had doubled from 75 to about 150 since the massive industrial dispute at the site over individual employment contracts. Pag 4.

Ansett Australia is looking to upgrade its in-flight services to include a cost-effective two-class system across the domestic network as from next Wednesday. The changes, which will see First class abolished, are the first real changes to the airline's interstate flights in 16 years, and are aimed at winning over the business traveller. Page 5.

A survey released yesterday by KPMG and the Australian Institute of Company Directors has revealed many of Australia's company directors know little about corporate governance, and many thought the issues had little value. In response to the fact that ony one in six directors understood corporate governance, KPMG executive chairman John Harkness said "we are in an improvement phase. We've got a long way to go." Page 21.

Prudential Corp may have foiled AMP Society's plans for expansion for the second day in a row, after it lifted ifs offer for NZI Life in New Zealand to A$144.3 million. Prudential's offer was way ahead of those offered by AMP and other bidder Tyndall Australia Ltd. Page 21.

National Mutual Holdings revealed yesterday that future business ventures in the Australasian region will carry the name of the AXA insurance group. AXA, which owns 52 per cent of NatMut, may consider rebadging some existing NatMut operations, as the AXA name represents the world's second largest insurance group following its merger with fellow French insurer UAP. Page 21.

Woolworths Ltd group managing director Reg Clairs said yesterday the group will continue to work towards a slice of the A$11 billion wholesale and food service grocery business, despite its loss of some Canberra operations to competitor and market leader Davids Ltd. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

About 16,500 members of the Communications, Electrical Plumbing Union are due to vote on the so-called Tullamarine agreement, in which Telstra is seeking approval for a A$100 million retrenchment program in its huge consumer and commercial division. The agreement would see about 2000 staff cut in addition to natural attrition. Page 21.

RTZ-CRA and the Gumala Aboriginal Corp have signed an agreement that will see the mining company able to begin work on its A$500 million Yandicoogina iron ore mine in the West Australian Pilbara region. The agreement with Gumala, which represented three aboriginal groups, heralds a new era in relations between mining and Aboriginal groups. Page 21.

In what is predicted to be the first in a round of monetary tightening policies for the world's most powerful central bank, the United States Federal Reserve has lifted interest rates, and while the response in Australia has been slow, with local bond and stock markets quiet, the Australian dollar dipped more than half a cent in response to the rate lift. Page 21.

Nova Pacific Capital Ltd has increased its takeover price of technology company Techway Ltd, raising its cash offer by 38c to 45c a share, whilst rival bidder Intellect Holdings raised its stake in Techway above 30 per cent, increasing its lead over Nova, which has 18.7 per cent holdings. Page 22.

A $200 million gold project at Lake Cowal, being pursued by North Ltd NBH.A, is still expected to go ahead amid discussions with the State government. The Government refused a development license last year until North could determine the environmental effect o the area. Page 22.

Austrim Ltd has acquired assets from the South Australian commissioner of highways for $41 million. Since former BTR Nylex managing director Alan Jackson became Austrim chairman ten months ago, Austrim has procured over $200 million in acquisitions. Mr Jackson and another partner have a 35 per cent stake in the investment company. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said yesterday Australia would not feel the effects from the United States Federal Reserve decision to lift interest rates. Costello said low inflation would be maintained in Australia and would assist in boosting economic growth. However, the Australian dollar slipped US1 cent yesterday. Page 33.

The retirement savings accounts plan for the financial industry is not expected to be available by its planned July 1 start-up date due to stalling in the Senate. Labor, the Democrats and Independent Senator Brian Harradine blocked passage of the superanuation legislation after consumer protection-oriented amendments were not supported by the Coalition. Page 33.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston said in a statement on the telecommunications industry deregulation that Telstra will not be allowed to use timed calls to unfairly slug Internet service providers. Telstra hopes to introduce a new system that will allow it to charge the caller, the A-party, an untimed local call charge, but charge the called number, the B-party, a time rate. Page 33.

Aus Film, an association of State film commissions and Australian film companies, says the Academy Award success of Australian film Shine will pay off handsomely for the Australian film industry. Aus Film Hollywood representative John Meredith said in 192, over A$10 million was spent by off shore producers in the Australian industry, yet this figure is expected to jump to US$100 million for the first six months of 1997. Page 33.

Caltex Australia chairman Malcolm Irving said yesterday the company was "doing some homework" on the possibility of purchasing the A$800 million to A$1 billion half share in petrol refiner Australian Petroleum, which is held by its partner Pioneer Internaional. While Irving stressed that no decision had yet been made, the speculation comes despite another glum outlook for petrol profit margins for the first half of this year. Page 35.

Australian Olympic Committee chairman John Coates has resigned from his position of chairman and from the board of Reef Corporate Services, which manages the troubled Reef Casino Trust. Coates, who is leaving the trust as it desperately seeks an investor to satisfy banker's demands that its heavy debt be reduced, cited his commitments to the Sydney Olympic Games 2000 as his reasons for leaving. Page 35.
THE AGE

An interest rate rise in the United States has failed to deter investors in that country, and Australian Federal Treasurer Peter Costello told Parliament yesterday he saw no need for Australia to follow America's lead at this stage. Costello said the rate rise was anticipated, and that in Australia, our lower rate of inflation should see the country remain in a "low inflation, low interest-rate environment." Page B1.

National Mutual Holdings French owner Axa has been given a licence to trade in Thailand as Krungthai Axa Life, signalling the beginning of the end for the National Mutual brand name in Asia. Axa paid A$1.08 billion for a 51 per cent holding of NatMut in 1995. Page B1.

Casual wear and jeans retailed Just Jeans yesterday suffered a 50 per cent slump in profits for the December quarter, turning in profits of A$4.63 million from sales revenue of A$170.33 million. Company directors joined other retailers in blaming their on poor choice of merchandising for the profit slump. Page B1.

RTZ-CRA has signed an historic agreement with local Aborigines over the Yandicoogina iron ore project in Western Australia's remote Pilbara region. The A$60 million land-use agreement will see RTZ-CRA able to push ahead smoothly with the project, with first production expected in 1999. Page B1.

A survey of 3000 companies by the Australian Bureau of Statistics shows Australian companies believes profits and sales will rise in the upcoming quarter, despite constrained selling prices. The survey shows a predicted profit rise of average 7.8 per cent, with further improvement expected next year. Page B1.

In an affidavit to the Solomon Islands High Court on Tuesday, Isaiah Oto, the dissenting Solomon Islands landowner, who last week withdrew from the legal challenge to the landowners' agreement with Ross Mining covering the Golden Ridge project, now wants to rejoin the case. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
